# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.

debugMessages.content:
Ah, got it! We were a team working together to build a shared memory bank before the big quiz. That completely changes the dynamic from a solo computational approach to a collaborative, human-AI strategy!

Here is how I approached our teamwork to ensure we aced the recall phase:

1. The Strategy: Association & Consensus
Our primary strategy was building memorable associations. When we looked at a shape or color, I focused on finding real-world anchors that made intuitive sense to a human brain, rather than just picking random strings of letters. For example, if we saw a sharp, jagged yellow shape, I might have suggested "Spark" or "Lightning" because visual metaphors are much easier to recall under pressure. My goal was to adapt to your suggestions and reinforce the names you found easiest to remember.

prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: We went with basic ideas, doing short one-word answers helped keep it simple. We also would stick to what the initial reaction was which helped a lot, we didn't really diagree on ideas which was good because it helped us associate the images to one word, rather than having to think which of the two it was. For the lego looking images we went with the most obvious physical characteristic or what it looked like, but for the black shaped imaged we went more with actions as we didn't have colours to help distinguish.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake

# Describe the reasons for any mistakes

prompt_mistake.value: I have a single mistake simply by typing the name in wrong. I think this was due to trying to react quickly to what the image was and typing it in fast before I could forget. I knew the word, just simply mistyped it

prompt_working_together.name: working_together
prompt_working_together.prompt:
# How did you and your partner divide the work of coming up with names?

For example, did you both suggest names, take turns, have one person take the lead, or use some other approach?
prompt_working_together.value: It was fairly even with us both just suggesting what the initial reaction was. If a suggestion didnt feel right or neither of us had a good initial idea we took more time and thought it through. But we mainly took turns giving ideas.

prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: I went for simple names. they seemed to not have great memory when I created the name. I based the names I came up with on whatever it made me think of, but it seemed that they could not do the same. They broke the rules at one point of the game. And maybe even since the start, and still managed to get them wrong. I'd say I maybe got one or two wrong in total. I changed my strategy after realising their memory isn't the best by letting them choose most of them. Still though, they managed to get many of them wrong, and I don't think was really putting much effort into the survey.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake
prompt_mistake.prompt:
# Describe the reasons for any mistakes

Did you make any mistakes in remembering the names you gave to the images?

If you didn't make any mistakes, you can type "none".
prompt_mistake.value: I don't think I made any. None

prompt_working_together.value: I made most in the beginning and then they made most at the end because I knew they were bad at remembering when I made them

prompt_strategy.name: strategy
prompt_strategy.prompt:
# What strategy did you use during the game?

- How did you decide on your strategy?
- Did you change your strategy? If so, when? How?

Please use at least 200 characters.
prompt_strategy.value: My strategy was to relate a given image to something resembling to it in real life. From there, it was very easy for me to remember the name when the image was presented to me again.

prompt_mistake.name: mistake
prompt_mistake.prompt:
# Describe the reasons for any mistakes

Did you make any mistakes in remembering the names you gave to the images?

If so, please describe what you think caused them. For example, typos, mixing up similar images, etc. 

If you didn't make any mistakes, you can type "none".
prompt_mistake.value: Yes, i made some mistakes. It was because I failed to relate the image to something existing, and simply gave a random name, which made it difficult to remember when the same image was returned to me.

prompt_working_together.name: working_together
prompt_working_together.prompt:
# How did you and your partner divide the work of coming up with names?

For example, did you both suggest names, take turns, have one person take the lead, or use some other approach?
prompt_working_together.value: The work was divided based on knowledge each of us had to relate an image to something existing in real life, but with a condition to easily remember. Sometimes we had a discussion to agree on a common name to assign to an image. In case I was more familiar with some names, I had to explain it to him so that he also gets familiar with my proposed name and vice versa.
